children: Gold prices received a powerful signal from a major reserve manager. The Peoples Bank of China added approximately 20.2 tonnes of bullion in August, extending its gold-buying streak to 22 consecutive months.
It was Chinas largest monthly addition since October 2023, despite elevated prices. That strongly suggests the central banks demand is strategic rather than dependent on cheaper entry points.
What the Buying Streak Means for Gold Prices
The PBOC added 650,000 ounces in August, lifting reserves to 76.73 million ounces. Additional metal and higher prices increased their reported value.
Chinas total foreign-exchange reserves also climbed to $3.4383 trillion at the end of August, rising $19.5 billion, or 0.57%, from July. It was the second consecutive monthly increase.

For gold investors, the most important number is not simply the 20.2-tonne purchase. It is the persistence behind it. Buying for 22 straight months indicates an ongoing effort to diversify national reserves, giving the bullion market a large source of recurring institutional demand.

That demand can support prices during periods when investment flows elsewhere weaken. It may also encourage other central banks seeking greater reserve diversification to maintain or expand their gold allocations.

However, Chinas purchases do not guarantee that gold will rise continuously. Bullion remains sensitive to real interest rates, the U.S. dollar, inflation expectations, exchange-traded fund flows, jewelry demand, and shifts in geopolitical risk. A stronger dollar or rising real yields could still pressure prices even while central banks accumulate.
The August increase is therefore best viewed as structural support rather than a short-term trading signal. China is demonstrating that elevated prices have not disrupted its buying program.

For investors, that reduces one major downside concern: the possibility that record prices would chase away an important buyer. Instead, the largest monthly purchase in nearly three years suggests official demand may remain resilient even when gold becomes more expensive.

title: Gold Prices Flash Strong Signal as Major Buyer Doubles Down
